candidate.title: Struc- / ture-Seq / DMS-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned central Illumina row labeled "Struc- / ture-Seq / DMS-Seq": in vivo DMS-treated and untreated-control branches, random-hexamer reverse transcription, linker ligation, PCR, and terminal DNA. The line break in Structure-seq is typographic. Neighboring SHAPE-MaP and SPARE rows are outside this record. This is a grouped explanatory schematic: its complete drawn random-hexamer route is supported for Structure-seq. The original DMS-seq paper supports the common DMS-to-RT-stop measurement principle but specifies a different RNA-fragment/adapter library interface. Applicability is resolved in method_scopes and corrections; the drawing is retained rather than silently replacing its route. Targeted Structure-Seq and other methods named on the catalogue page are background, not additional targets. The record ends at the drawn DNA libraries; sequencing is used only to explain what those libraries represent.

operations.label: +DMS / In vivo treatment
operations.description: Treat in vivo RNA with DMS; exposed A/C sites acquire the orange modifications shown in the upper branch. The initial structural cartoon is explanatory, not a preceding RNA-processing step.
operations.mechanism: DMS methylates the accessible Watson-Crick base-pairing faces of unpaired A and C; the figure caption specifies A/C in loops.
operations.information_effect: Chemical marks record base accessibility at probing. Reactivity supports an accessible/unpaired interpretation; protection can also arise from RNA-binding proteins, so lack of signal is not a unique proof of base pairing.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Use the supplied random hexamers on RNA from the treated sample to synthesize DNA. Extension arrests at DMS-modified sites, yielding the shortened lime products drawn on the RNA templates. This local random-hexamer interface is assigned to Structure-seq.

operations.information_effect: Converts an RNA accessibility mark into a cDNA termination boundary while copying RNA sequence. The boundary provides positional evidence for the probed site rather than encoding a mutation.

method_scopes.rationale: The central-row title groups two targets, but the candidate collection page has the matching heading and explicitly captions this drawing "A schematic overview of Structure-seq." Its random-hexamer RT and cDNA-linker/PCR route is supported by the Structure-seq protocol abstract and the secondary catalogue paragraph. All eight local operations apply to this depicted Structure-seq implementation, with treated/control RT, ligation and PCR represented separately. Structure-seq and the poster capitalization Structure-Seq denote the same named method here; this is not a claim that every family implementation has identical preparation. The original 2014 paper is identified and assessed at abstract level, and the 2015 protocol is a separate supporting protocol publication.

method_scopes.rationale: DMS-seq is a genuine co-target of the assigned poster title and its Rouskin citation identifies PMID 24336214. The common in vivo DMS probing and untreated comparator are directly applicable. The primary full text resolves the library-interface difference: DMS-seq randomly fragments and size-selects modified RNA, ligates an adapter to RNA before RT, selects prematurely terminated cDNAs, circularizes cDNA, and adds Illumina adapters by PCR. This supports the same purpose correspondence of DMS accessibility marks -> RT-stop positions -> sequenced DNA, not identical local preparation. The drawn rt_dms/rt_control instances require random-hexamer inputs; ligate_dms/ligate_control and pcr_dms/pcr_control inherit those cDNA inputs. None of those six fixed-history local instances is assigned to original DMS-seq. Their drawn paths are retained as Structure-seq, while the DMS-seq correspondence is recorded here and in corrections rather than adding an unshown complete workflow. The DMS-seq terminal DNA readout measures relative site reactivity through the mapped ends of selected RT-termination products, as stated in b00003 and b00018.

corrections.diagram_observation: The poster groups Structure-seq and DMS-seq beside one two-branch scheme. In its treated branch, the "Random hexamers" arrow feeds reverse transcription of DMS-marked RNA, followed by "Ligate linker", "PCR", and "DNA".
corrections.primary_statement: The original DMS-seq implementation in Rouskin et al. instead fragments modified RNA and ligates an RNA 3′ adapter before RT, then selects truncated cDNAs; library generation subsequently circularizes cDNA and adds Illumina adapters by PCR. This paper-supported interpretation restricts rt_dms and its fixed-history descendants ligate_dms and pcr_dms to the depicted Structure-seq route. DMS-seq retains the chemical-probing/RT-stop purpose correspondence but does not inherit the drawn random-hexamer library interface.
